items.instructions: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word on the left.

explanation.en: At the end of a list, and so on shows that there are more items that you have not named.
Loads of is an informal way to say a great many or a large amount of.
Roughly is a vague way to give a number that is not exact: roughly forty people.
Sort of softens a statement, as somewhat does: It was sort of annoying.
A bit of is informal for a small amount of: a bit of luck.

items.prompt: an informal word for an object whose name you cannot remember

explanation.en: Thingy replaces the name of something you cannot remember: Pass me that thingy.

items.prompt: used to show that a word is not meant completely literally

explanation.en: So to speak warns the listener that the word is being used figuratively.

items.prompt: used at the end of a list to show there are more items you have not mentioned

explanation.en: And so on suggests that the list could continue in the same way.

items.prompt: used after a guess to show you are not sure it is correct

explanation.en: In She works in banking or something, the speaker is not sure about the detail.

items.prompt: added informally to a time or an adjective to mean approximately

explanation.en: -ish gives an approximate meaning: seven-ish means about seven o'clock; greenish means a little green.
